## Summary
Document the ownership model and the expected show/hide behavior for the Gym SLL demo.

## User impact
Contributors can follow the documented pattern instead of adding more ad hoc chrome visibility logic.

## Minimal End-to-End Slice
- **Code**: No runtime code beyond doc-snippet consistency checks.
- **Tests**: Ensure any referenced commands or snippets match the real test targets.
- **Docs**: Update `example-games/gym/README.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` with ownership/visibility guidance.
- **Infra**: Reuse the existing docs structure.
- **Observability**: Document how to confirm visibility behavior in the browser demo.

## Existing implementation to reuse
- Gym SLL sections in `example-games/gym/README.md`
- SLL guidance in `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
- browser tests for the Gym demo

## Acceptance Criteria
- Docs explain which mode shows which chrome.
- Docs explain how to register objects as shell-owned or scene-owned.
- Docs mention that Scene-only suppresses shared shell chrome.
- Documentation changes match the implemented behavior.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: Gym scene wiring (CG-0MPFM2MM4003OPP8).
- Parent: Suppress shared Gym help chrome in pure scene-only SLL views (CG-0MPFLM5EB009N5X8).

## Goal

As a player, I want the closing screen to distinguish the voyage I actually made — including quitting early — so that the epilogue score means something.

Found during the spike observation log (`docs/gym/long-erasure-observation-log.md`, §4.4 / §2, `CG-0MWNHZEGJ0099JFM`): the epilogue grants the **full arc award (60 points) for entering any ending card**, including the deliberately terminal `Abandon the voyage` reached in Act II.

Measured (named routes, `npx tsx scripts/long-erasure-playtest.ts`):

- `abandon` (5 choices, 6 beats, ~80 words of prose, 9 clock left): score **79** — arc 60 + choices 10 + resources 13 − losses 4 → band "A voyage that left a mark", 4 points below finishing.
- `reset-cheap` (7 choices, 8 beats, ~106 words, 4 clock left): score **83** — arc 60 + choices 12 + resources 15 − losses 4 → top band.
- 56 of 160 policy runs took the abandon hatch; every one lands in (or immediately below) the top band.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Abandoning the voyage in Act II can no longer score in the top band: the arc component must reflect the acts *played*, not the ending card entered (e.g. arc credit only for acts advanced beyond, and a reduced/zero arc award for an `abandon` outcome).
- A finishing route still outscores the abandon terminal by a clear margin (>= 15 points), asserted by a unit test on `scoreRun` / `buildEpilogue` in `tests/gym/`.
- The band labels and the documented score table in `GymLongErasureGame.ts` stay consistent with the new rule, and the scene help text's epilogue description still holds.
- `npx tsx scripts/long-erasure-playtest.ts --seeds 40 --route "abandon=…"` reports the abandon route in a band below the finishing routes.

## Key Files

- `example-games/gym/GymLongErasureGame.ts` (`JOURNEY_SCORE_TABLE`, `scoreRun`, `enterCard` act bookkeeping)
- `tests/gym/GymLongErasureGame.test.ts`, `tests/gym/LongErasureEpilogue.test.ts`
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymLongErasureScene.ts` (help text)
- `scripts/long-erasure-playtest.ts` (verification harness)
- `docs/gym/long-erasure-observation-log.md` (§4.4 / §7)

## Notes

Discovered from `CG-0MWNHZEGJ0099JFM` (observation log). This is the measured evidence behind the GDD question "must endings be distinguishable?" (`CG-0MWNFVLYT003M7XF`); fixing it here keeps the Gym spike honest as a demonstrator, and the same rule should inform the full game's epilogue.
data.title: Gym Long Erasure: epilogue must not award full arc credit for abandoning the voyage

data.description:
## Goal

Make the epilogue's arc component reflect the acts a run actually played, so abandoning the voyage cannot
collect the Act III award — the implementation half of parent `CG-0MWNSR376002QBY9`.

Root cause (measured): `enterCard` credits every act up to the `Ending` rank on entering *any* ending card
(`recordActsBefore(working, ACT_RANK.Ending)`), so `Abandon the voyage` — entered from Act II at
`le-ii-offer` — collects the full 60 arc points. The fix credits the acts played through: a run that ends
credits the act it was in when it ended, so an abandon from Act II credits Acts I–II (35) while a finishing
run from Act III still credits Acts I–III (60).

Predicted authoring-content outcomes with the rule: abandon 54 ("A voyage the erasure nearly kept", two bands
below the top), reset-cheap 83 (top band, unchanged), expiry unchanged (no credit for the unplayed beat).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `enterCard` no longer credits arc for the `Ending` rank itself: a run that reaches an ending credits exactly the acts it played through (the act the ending beat was entered from), so the authored abandon credits `['I', 'II']` (arc 35) and every finishing ending credits `['I', 'II', 'III']` (arc 60).
- The rule is content-agnostic: `GymLongErasureGame.ts` contains no reference to the abandon ending's id (`le-end-abandon`) or its label; crediting derives only from `ACT_RANK` and the run's current act, so any future ending reached from Act II inherits the rule.
- The no-successor terminal close path in `chooseOption` applies the same rule (both close paths agree), proven by a unit test over a minimal hand-built `LongErasureContent` fixture whose terminal option pushes no card.
- Act gating (`'backward-act'`), clock expiry (`outcome: 'expired'`, which credits nothing for the unplayed beat), reset detection (`outcome: 'reset'`) and the `[0, 100]` clamp are unchanged, and the existing module + epilogue suites pass without edits to their expectations.
- The `JOURNEY_SCORE_TABLE` docblock states the new `arc` rule and keeps the "authored content tops out at 92 (60 + 12 + 20)" sentence true; no weight, cap, band threshold or band label changes.
- The sibling test item's regression cases go from red to green, and the changed-scope unit suite (`/skill:test --type unit`) plus `npm run build` pass before the commit.

**Key Files:**

- `example-games/gym/GymLongErasureGame.ts` (`enterCard`, `recordActsBefore`, `chooseOption`, `JOURNEY_SCORE_TABLE`)
- `tests/gym/GymLongErasureEpilogue.test.ts`
- `tests/gym/GymLongErasureGame.test.ts`

**Covers parent AC:** "the arc component must reflect the acts *played*, not the ending card entered".
data.title: Long Erasure: credit only played acts when a run ends

## Summary

Write the GDD's presentation and technical contract: SLL zone names for every surface, overlay and HUD behaviour, audio/SFX mapping, accessibility, and determinism, save/load, transcript and replay expectations.

## Target outcome

An implementer knows which SLL zones and HUD components to use and which events must be animated and sounded, so the game is consistent with every other TCE game on day one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- UI surfaces are specified with SLL zone names for each surface (resource HUD, act/scene banner, objective panel, choice list, journal, epilogue screen), with no absolute pixel coordinates.
- Overlay behaviour is specified for help, settings, journal and confirmation, following the project's depth-ordered overlay convention.
- Audio and SFX mapping is specified with `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` names per event, plus the reduced-motion alternative for each animated event.
- Accessibility is specified: reduced motion, verbosity and tooltips, colour-independent signalling, and keyboard and touch input paths.
- Determinism, save/load, transcript and replay expectations are stated: seeded RNG, serialisation version, transcript event set and replay determinism.
- Every surface or capability named is either already available in the engine or listed in the engine-gap backlog.

## Minimal Implementation

- Write one table per concern with the engine API or zone name in the right-hand column.
- Cite the existing Gym scene that demonstrates each pattern.
- Mark every unavailable capability as a backlog pointer, not a promise.

## Risky assumptions

- The GDD proposes surfaces that do not exist yet (act/scene transition presentation). Each must be explicit as a gap.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the GDD foundation and the resource model.

## Key Files

- `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` — the presentation and technical sections.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — SLL, HUD, audio and replay references to cite.
- `docs/SFX_CONVENTION.md` — the SFX key convention.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymLongErasureScene.ts` — the spike's rendered surface.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymOverlayUiScene.ts` — the overlay and clipping reference.

## Impact

An implementer can build the game's presentation by zone name and SFX key instead of inventing a layout and an audio map.
data.title: GDD presentation contract: UI, audio, accessibility, determinism
